Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
41-year-old male with 2-month history of fatigue, poor sleep, low mood, decreased libido, and exertional dyspnea; hypothyroidism on thyroxine. Plan for in-person review and blood work.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Increasing tiredness, difficulty getting up, low daytime energy for ~2 months (coinciding with new job).  
• Associated symptoms: Poor appetite, insomnia, difficulty concentrating, low mood, reduced sex drive, exertional shortness of breath.  
• Pertinent negatives: Denies suicidal ideation or self-harm thoughts; no vision changes.  
• Past medical history: Hypothyroidism.  
• Medications: Thyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: No medication allergies reported.  
• Family history: Father died by suicide 15 years ago; otherwise non-contributory.  
• Social: Married; recently started new job (~2 months ago).

Examination:
• No in-consultation physical exam performed.  
• Vitals: Not recorded.

Impression:
• Fatigue, low mood, decreased libido, and exertional dyspnea in patient with treated hypothyroidism – differential to include thyroid dysfunction, depression, anemia, and other metabolic causes.

Plan:
• Arrange face-to-face GP appointment within next few days for full physical examination.  
• Order blood tests (details not specified; likely thyroid panel and baseline screening per GP assessment).  
• Reassure patient; confirmed no current suicidal thoughts.  
• Follow-up after investigations to review results and management options.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Full medication list (only thyroxine mentioned); dosing details; comprehensive allergies (environmental/food); lifestyle factors (smoking, alcohol, exercise baseline); review of systems beyond discussed points.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially implied absence of morning erections recently, then stated no change – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor freezes but content understandable.
